outcome.technical: DESIGN. A base step that runs a declared entry over some suites is named base_suites_step_name(declared, suites) = joined_step_name(declared, ['affected/base: A, B']), using the existing joined grammar with a new arm DERIVED_BASE_ARM='base' (no arm in _affected_tests.ARMS, pinned by bfs4). So derived_step_suites/step_runs_suite know exactly which suites it ran, while its name is never the entry's, so base_step (_evidence_io.py, the name+verbatim-command matcher, unchanged) never takes it for the whole step. That is the invariant: a per-suite step cannot answer for a suite it did not run (bsu4). API, _evidence_io.py: DERIVED_BASE_ARM, base_suites_step_name, base_suites_of(name) -> (declared, suites)|None, suite_base_step(base_steps, step, suite) (same name, suite listed, step_answered, and where both carry a command, _same_call_over: base command minus listed suites == red command word for word), suite_base_run(rows, head, task_id, step, suite) (newest clean-tree run at head, not task's own, holding one: the (commit, suite) key), private _suites_unmeasured, plus import shlex. base_unmeasured: a whole-step base of the name still answers first; a declared red step naming its failing suites (not cut) is answered per suite once any clean run at head holds a per-suite base step of its name, returning '<name>: <suite>' for suites no run answered; otherwise it falls back to the old whole-step reading, so every existing row reads exactly as before (kb/bs/js/rh blocks green). base_row_for: code unchanged, docstring corrected (base_unmeasured no longer makes only its selection). _affected_tests.py: is_bare_spelling(spelling, command) (shell words == spelling minus its single {paths} word) and is_bare_entry(entry, phase, meta) (build key resolved, recorded spelling only). PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: one paragraph in each module's section.
